title: Landscaping
guideTip: Work with nature — always plan before you dig or plant anything!

scenarios.title: Wilting Flower Bed
scenarios.description: The new flower bed has drooping, wilting plants — they look terrible!
scenarios.hint: Check the soil first — stick your finger in. Is it dry or wet?

scenarios.title: Patchy Lawn
scenarios.description: The play area has ugly bare dirt patches where grass won't grow.
scenarios.hint: Rake first to loosen the soil — then seed, then water gently.

scenarios.title: Overgrown Hedge
scenarios.description: The garden hedge has grown wild and is blocking the path.
scenarios.hint: Gloves first — trim from the top down for a neat, even shape.

scenarios.title: Muddy Garden Path
scenarios.description: Rain turned the garden path into a muddy, slippery mess.
scenarios.hint: Add mulch or gravel — it improves drainage and looks great too!

scenarios.title: Weed Invasion
scenarios.description: Weeds have taken over the vegetable garden bed!
scenarios.hint: Gloves on — pull weeds when soil is wet so roots come out fully.

scenarios.title: Poor Drainage Zone
scenarios.description: After rain, water pools in one area for days — roots will rot!
scenarios.hint: Improve drainage with better soil and a gentle slope away from plants.

scenarios.title: New Vegetable Bed
scenarios.description: Plan and plant a new vegetable bed for the season.
scenarios.hint: Measure first — know the space before you dig or plant anything!

scenarios.title: Soil Needs Nutrients
scenarios.description: The vegetable bed soil is hard, dry, and producing poorly.
scenarios.hint: Add compost and mix it in deeply — healthy soil makes healthy plants.

scenarios.title: Erosion on Slope
scenarios.description: Heavy rain is washing soil off the hillside into the path below.
scenarios.hint: Plant ground cover immediately — roots hold soil in place!

scenarios.title: Tree Root Damage
scenarios.description: A tree root is cracking the garden path and needs addressing.
scenarios.hint: Plan carefully — cutting roots wrong can kill the tree.

tiers.title: Advanced
tiers.reviewNote: Advanced landscaping includes irrigation, erosion, slope, and drainage design that may require site-specific professional review.

title: Community Service
guideTip: Helping others is one of the greatest skills you will ever develop in life!

scenarios.title: Garden Cleanup Day
scenarios.description: The community garden is full of trash after a storm. Neighbors need help!
scenarios.hint: Organize before starting — sorted waste is easier to dispose of properly.

scenarios.title: Elderly Neighbor Needs Help
scenarios.description: Your elderly neighbor's garden is overgrown — they can't do it anymore.
scenarios.hint: Showing up with a smile and willingness means the world to someone.

actions.label: Make them fill out a form

scenarios.title: Plant Trees for the Park
scenarios.description: The community park has no shade — elders and kids suffer in summer heat.
scenarios.hint: Organize a planting day — many hands make light work together!

actions.label: Say someone else will do it
Wait for the city to act

scenarios.title: Food Drive
scenarios.description: Many families in the community don't have enough food this week.
scenarios.hint: Collect, sort, and deliver — every single can makes a real difference.

scenarios.title: Welcome New Neighbors
scenarios.description: A family just moved in next door and looks overwhelmed and lonely.
scenarios.hint: A simple welcome makes an enormous difference to someone new.

actions.label: Give them a list of rules

tiers.title: Intermediate
tiers.reviewNote: Intermediate and advanced community scenarios include disputes, flood response, safety planning, fundraising, and governance decisions.

title: Cooking & Nutrition
guideTip: Good food starts with good ingredients — fresh, whole foods feed the body and mind!

scenarios.title: Kitchen Safety First
scenarios.description: You're about to cook for the first time. What do you do FIRST?
scenarios.hint: Wash your hands — clean hands prevent food poisoning!

scenarios.title: Knife Safety
scenarios.description: You need to chop vegetables for a salad. What is the safe way?
scenarios.hint: Curl your fingers under — the 'bear claw' grip protects your fingertips!

actions.label: Bear claw grip + cut away from body
Hold the knife at the tip

scenarios.title: Balanced Meal Planning
scenarios.description: Plan a healthy lunch that has protein, vegetables, and carbohydrates.
scenarios.hint: Think colors — a colorful plate almost always means a balanced plate!

scenarios.title: Safe Food Storage
scenarios.description: Leftover cooked chicken has been sitting out for 4 hours. What do you do?
scenarios.hint: The danger zone is 40-140°F for 2+ hours — bacteria multiply fast!

actions.label: Put it in the fridge now
Eat it — looks fine to me

scenarios.title: Reading a Recipe
scenarios.description: The recipe says to preheat the oven to 350°F. Why do you do this FIRST?
scenarios.hint: Preheating ensures even cooking from the moment food goes in the oven!

actions.label: Skip it — ovens heat fast enough
Put food in then turn on oven
